boards.title: Your First Weekend at Montclair State University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend loop: get oriented, find campus resources, add art and movement, and end with a campus activity.

cards.title: Begin at Montclair Heights Station
cards.subtitle: Arrival and campus orientation
cards.notes: Use the station as a clear starting point, then open the interactive campus map for walking directions to your next named destination.
cards.short_summary: A transit-linked starting point for a self-guided campus loop.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair Heights Station is identified on Montclair State’s official campus map.
cards.access_notes: Check NJ Transit service and fare information before travel.

cards.title: Check the Student Center calendar
cards.subtitle: Find a current campus event
cards.notes: Pause at the Student Center and Annex, then use the Student Engagement calendar to choose an event that fits your weekend.
cards.short_summary: A practical planning stop for current student programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Office of Student Engagement publishes an events calendar, and the Student Center and Annex is a campus-map location.
cards.source_title: Events Calendar – Office of Student Engagement
cards.access_notes: Individual events may have registration, eligibility, or capacity requirements.

cards.title: Locate Café Diem
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library, first floor
cards.notes: Make this a short refresh stop while learning the library layout; Café Diem is listed on the first floor of Sprague Library.
cards.short_summary: A named campus café paired with library orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair State lists Café Diem on the first floor of Sprague Library.
cards.access_notes: Food and beverages require purchase unless another campus program states otherwise.

cards.title: Settle into Sprague Library
cards.subtitle: Books, media, study rooms, and research help
cards.notes: Find a study spot, browse the catalog, or ask a librarian a question; reserve a study space if your group needs one.
cards.short_summary: A weekend reset with academic resources close at hand.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries provides book and media search, study-space reservations, and librarian assistance at Sprague Library.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library’s current hours and room-reservation rules before visiting.

cards.title: See what’s on at the Segal Gallery
cards.subtitle: Red Hawk Parking Deck, fourth floor
cards.notes: Check the exhibition schedule before heading over, then take in the gallery at your own pace and use its digital guide if useful.
cards.short_summary: A free campus-gallery visit with a documented location.
cards.evidence_claim: The George Segal Gallery is on the fourth floor of the Red Hawk Parking Deck; University Galleries admission is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The gallery’s listed public hours are Tuesday–Friday, 12–4 p.m., with select Saturdays and appointments; confirm an exhibition is open.

cards.title: Walk by the Amphitheater
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Alexander Kasser Theater
cards.notes: Add the stone amphitheater to an outdoor campus walk; check the university calendar if you want to pair the visit with a performance.
cards.short_summary: A historic outdoor performance venue on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2,000-seat Amphitheater, originally constructed in 1940, is used for performances, festivals, classes, and special events.
cards.access_notes: Event attendance and access depend on the scheduled program; do not enter closed production areas.

cards.title: Browse the Kasser display cases
cards.subtitle: Alexander Kasser Theater lobby
cards.notes: Look for the rotating exhibition display cases in the lobby, then check the gallery page for current viewing access before making the walk.
cards.short_summary: A small arts stop inside a named campus theater.
cards.evidence_claim: University Galleries presents exhibitions in display cases on the ground and mezzanine levels of the Alexander Kasser Theater lobby.
cards.access_notes: The page lists fall and spring public hours of Monday–Friday, 12–6 p.m.; the cases may also be viewable when the box office is open.

cards.title: Plan a Rec Center session
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation
cards.notes: Choose a current recreation program or simply get familiar with the facility; bring your Montclair State ID for entry and follow facility rules.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop for an active part of the weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation says the Student Recreation Center provides events, programs, and resources, and requires a Montclair State ID swipe for entry.
cards.source_title: In Person & Virtual Programming – Campus Recreation
cards.access_notes: Only individuals swiping a Montclair State University ID may enter; verify current hours and program requirements.

cards.title: Take a campus ice-skating break
cards.subtitle: 1 Arena Drive, Little Falls
cards.notes: Check the public-skate schedule, then bring your Montclair State ID to use the student rental and skating option described by Campus Recreation.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus arena with student skating access.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation states that public skating sessions are offered and that rental and skating are free for MSU students.
cards.source_title: Montclair State University Ice Arena – Campus Recreation
cards.access_notes: Confirm the specific public-skate session before going; the university lists normal arena hours as Monday–Sunday, 6 a.m.–midnight.

cards.title: Finish with the outdoor sculptures
cards.subtitle: Campus public-art walk
cards.notes: Use the gallery’s campus information to spot public art outdoors, and take a phone photo only where it does not disrupt people or events.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced outdoor art activity to close the loop.
cards.evidence_claim: University Galleries maintains public art installed throughout the campus, including outdoor sculptures.
cards.access_notes: Remain on public paths and observe any temporary event or installation restrictions.
